blocking_objections: gemini-3-1-pro: Premise P4 cites 'V5' as its verification evidence, but V5 is completely missing from the Verification Log (Section 16).

oc-glm-5-3: Load-bearing premise P4 (retrospective contamination — the sole basis for the E4 gate, the CONTAMINATED-PENDING default in §8/AC13, and the `.git`-free export / no-history-clone prohibition in P3-B) cites verification row "V5", but §16 contains no V5 entry: the log jumps V4 → V6a/V6b → V7a/b → V9 → V10 → V11 (V8 is also absent, though uncited). No surviving §16 row quotes the diagnosis-bearing row-114 text at `world-mission.md:1891` that P4 claims was "read directly" — the doc's most consequential factual claim is therefore asserted, not verified, which violates gate 1 and is precisely the "shorthand premise log" defect this r3 was scoped to eliminate. P8 (row-92 artifact F-5 caveats) is likewise unmapped to any §16 row despite the premise-table contract "verified while authoring → §16".

oc-kimi-k3: The protocol's two load-bearing execution prerequisites are admitted-UNKNOWN rather than verified, and the author concedes the searches that would settle them were never run on the roots that would answer them. PR (§5) mandates an ALREADY-EXISTING facility that enforces GET-only method/path policy 'independently of credentials and server authorization' and forbids building one (D6, §13 non-goals); E3 requires a positively DECLARED capture corpus. Yet V4 states 'the agent-runtime/fleet roots that would own one were NOT searched (declared missing roots)' and V10 states the method-filter search 'is NOT exhaustive absence proof. Existing external enforcement availability is UNKNOWN.' Under premise-verification, the decisive feasibility premises (does a confinement facility exist? does a capture cohort exist?) are therefore unverified exactly where the doc's own completion gate (§8/AC9: ≥3 qualifying successes, each requiring PR-passed plus a live walk) depends on them. As written, every attempt is structurally terminal at NOT-RUN(ISOLATION) or NOT-RUN(NO-CORPUS), so the row cannot reach its own acceptance criteria — the doc itself half-concedes this ('park explicitly'), which means it is requesting a fresh full author-excluding quorum for a protocol it predicts cannot execute. That is a design-doc defect, not an audit finding: quorum effort should not be spent until the UNKNOWN is resolved into either a positively identified facility/cohort (pinned in §PR/E3) or an explicit PARKED status.
